descripcion: At B1 you speculate with may, might and probably to talk about what might happen. The full speculation chain used at C1 comes later — a simple, graded prediction naming how sure you are is enough here.

ejemplos.texto: It might rain later, so take a jacket.
This will probably take a while.
It's definitely going to be busy tomorrow.

notas: Might and may express a real but uncertain possibility.
Probably usually goes between the subject and the verb: it will probably rain.
Definitely is used for a very confident prediction.

contraste.es: El español expresa predicción con el futuro simple o quizás/probablemente, lo cual se transfiere bien a estas formas inglesas de certeza graduada.

errores: Using will for everything, without varying the certainty.
Using definitely for something that's actually uncertain.
autochequeo: Have I used more than one certainty word, not just will?
Is probably in the right position?
Does the certainty level match how sure I really am?
Does the phrase sound polite and natural?
Does the phrase sound polite and natural?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the words used to express certainty in a prediction. Check the position of probably and whether the level of certainty is accurate. Do not rewrite the text.
